meetings.headline: Commission heard that enforcing demolition by neglect means court, and agreed to ask Town Council about a fines option.
meetings.summary: The commission met with the building commissioner (by Zoom) about how the district bylaw's demolition-by-neglect provisions can actually be enforced. He said the only mechanism is court action approved by the select board, and suggested asking Town Council whether fines under a zoning-style enforcement section could be added for the district. The members also discussed a Town Hall chimney bid, the master plan steering committee, a draft owner brochure, and ideas for historic signs and a walking tour.

what_happened.line: The commission declined to support reconsidering its denial of the 30 School Street window application, which the Select Board had asked it to revisit.
Members said they would approve it only if the replacement windows were removed, and asked that the new architect meet with them.
The commission re-voted the October and November minutes after the December meeting was found not properly posted; no December minutes will be posted.

why_it_matters: The window replacement at 30 School Street is a town capital project, and members said the cost estimate may be old and the budget may not cover all the windows, so the scope or the funding could come back to residents at a later town meeting.
A clearer, documented application process affects any property owner in the Architectural Preservation District who needs the commission's approval for exterior work.
